scope: The pinned July 19 npm calibration targets rescanned on October 5 local time (October 6 UTC). This is not an updated popularity ranking, malicious-package recall evaluation, or adjudicated accuracy claim.
notes: All 1000 requested attempts were recorded; 989 produced verdicts and 11 timed out. Error cases are excluded from successful-scan rates.
A successful scan here means a guard report was returned, not that all source or behavior was analyzed. Coverage gaps remain REVIEW findings.
All 35 blocks carry known-vulnerability findings; these are not malware labels. Zero heuristic block candidates is not an adjudicated false-positive rate.
Review categories overlap. Each package appears in exactly one of the 70 category-combination groups.
Citation availability measures retained file and snippet fields, not analysis completeness. Human review time and time saved were not measured.
The October 4 baseline used an earlier engine. Differences also include time-dependent registry metadata and vulnerabilities; they do not establish a causal accuracy improvement.
The revision, runner hash, and supplied engine build ID identify the scan as executed, before subsequent code changes.
Per-package names, verdicts, and source citations are excluded. The local review queue was verified against all raw records and retained with mode 0600.
